# Mechanism Requirements Quality Checklist: P-RF08 — Proactive insights (mechanism)

**Purpose**: Validate that the trigger/concurrency, lifecycle-reset, and failure-silence requirements for RF08's proactive-insight mechanism are complete, unambiguous, consistent, and measurable before implementation.
**Created**: 2026-10-22
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Trigger Condition Completeness & Clarity

- [ ] CHK001 Is the precise boundary for "a new multiple of N=5" specified unambiguously — e.g., does the 5th message itself satisfy the crossing, or only a subsequent one? [Clarity, Spec §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK002 Is it specified whether the user-message count (FR-001a) includes messages currently retrying/in the error state, or only messages that completed successfully? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK003 Is "foregrounded" used with a single, consistent meaning between the trigger definitions (§FR-001) and the pause/resume rule (§FR-010), or could a reader infer two different conditions? [Consistency, Spec §FR-001, §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK004 Is the minimum uniqueness guarantee for `triggerKey` (e.g., unique per trigger type and per session) stated explicitly, rather than left entirely to the implementation to decide? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002, Assumptions]

## Concurrency & Suspension Requirements

- [ ] CHK005 When the "turn not idle" deferral (§FR-003) and the "attempt in flight" suspension (§FR-004) could both apply at once, is the relationship between the two rules (which one governs, or how they compose) specified? [Gap, Spec §FR-003, §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK006 Is the "defer until idle" requirement (§FR-003) stated for both trigger types, or does its wording apply unambiguously to only one of them? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003]
- [ ] CHK007 Is the outcome specified for an inactivity window reaching 2 minutes while a message-count-triggered attempt is already in flight — is that inactivity occurrence dropped, queued, or re-evaluated after resume? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK008 Does "suspended — neither counted nor timed" (§FR-004) specify whether progress already accrued before suspension (partial count, partial elapsed time) is preserved or discarded once trigger evaluation resumes? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK009 Are the trigger-resumption requirements worded identically across all three resolution paths — dismissal (§FR-008), failure (§FR-006), and offline-skip (§FR-007) — so a reader cannot infer that resumption behaves differently depending on which path was taken? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004, §FR-006, §FR-007, §FR-008]

## Lifecycle, Reset & Non-Persistence

- [ ] CHK010 Is "viewing session" defined with enough precision to be distinguished consistently from "conversation" and from an app-level session throughout the spec? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009, Key Entities]
- [ ] CHK011 Is it specified whether the message-count and inactivity counters survive a session-expiry re-authentication (RF03/RF07 overlay), or whether they reset to zero as part of that recovery? [Gap, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK012 Does the "Novo Chat" edge case specify that *both* trigger conditions' counters start at zero for the new conversation, or only one of them by implication? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK013 Is "app restart" (§FR-009) treated consistently with "backgrounding the app" (§FR-010) as both being covered by the same reset/pause rules, or could a reader read them as two independently-specified behaviors that happen to overlap? [Consistency, Spec §FR-009, §FR-010]

## Failure & Offline Silence

- [ ] CHK014 Are all four failure modes — transport error, timeout, a 200 response with `status: 'failed'`, and an offline skip — specified with identical required behavior, with no wording difference that could imply one of them is treated differently? [Consistency, Spec §FR-006, §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK015 Is the connectivity signal used to determine "offline" for §FR-007's purposes named or cross-referenced, or is it left entirely implicit via the RF04 dependency? [Dependency, Spec §FR-007, Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK016 Is a maximum wait/timeout duration specified for an in-flight insight call before it must be treated as failed, or is this left undefined? [Gap, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK017 Is the boundary between the allowed client-side loading placeholder (Assumptions, ">300ms") and the "no visible indicator of any kind" prohibition (§FR-006, User Story 3) drawn clearly enough that the two requirements cannot be read as contradicting each other? [Ambiguity, Spec Assumptions, §FR-006]

## Dismissal & UI-State Isolation

- [ ] CHK018 Is "no other screen state changes" (§FR-008) specific enough to be objectively checked, or does "any other screen state" leave room for subjective judgment about what counts as screen state? [Measurability, Spec §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK019 Is the outcome specified for a dismissal action that is initiated at the same instant a new trigger condition becomes satisfied (race between dismissal completing and re-arming)? [Edge Case, Gap]

## Acceptance Criteria Measurability

- [ ] CHK020 Do SC-001 and SC-002's "100% of tested cases" define, or point to, a test population/sample size sufficient to make the criterion objectively verifiable rather than aspirational? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001, §SC-002]
- [ ] CHK021 Is SC-006's "no conversation ever shows more than one card... at the same time" worded consistently with FR-004's "at most one... per conversation at any time," or do the two differ in scope (e.g., per-conversation vs. global)? [Consistency, Spec §SC-006, §FR-004]

## Scenario & Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK022 Is a requirement defined for the device transitioning from offline to online while a trigger condition is pending but not yet satisfied (as opposed to the already-covered case of the device being offline *at* satisfaction)? [Edge Case, Gap]
- [ ] CHK023 Is the outcome specified for both trigger types becoming satisfied at the same instant (e.g., the 5th message also lands exactly at the 2-minute idle mark)? [Edge Case, Gap]
- [ ] CHK024 Is simultaneous viewing of the same conversation from more than one device/session addressed, or explicitly called out as out of scope? [Gap, Assumption]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK025 Is RF04's "idle turn" state cross-referenced precisely enough (e.g., naming the specific state values) that FR-003 can be evaluated without consulting RF04's own spec to resolve ambiguity? [Dependency, Spec §FR-003, Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK026 Is the assumption that the insight endpoint "never returns an HTTP error" (Assumptions) called out as depending on the backend contract remaining unchanged, so a future contract change would be flagged against this spec? [Assumption, Spec Assumptions]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [ ] CHK027 Do §FR-004 and the first Edge Cases bullet use fully consistent wording for "at most one attempt in flight / one card awaiting dismissal," or does any phrasing difference leave room for divergent implementations? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004, §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK028 Does any acceptance scenario or success criterion implicitly call for UI not otherwise specified (e.g., a loading indicator) in a way that could conflict with FR-011's exclusion list? [Conflict, Spec §FR-011]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
